title: Edvard Grieg's birth chart
metaDescription: Edvard Grieg's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 23.6° Gemini. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Venus and Saturn sit 0.3° from an exact trine — near enough that the tradition reads taste and structure as a single working part. The scheme reads trines as water finding its level: effortless, and invisible to the person living it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 23.6° Gemini. That falls in the third decan, 20°–30°, sub-ruled by Saturn in the classical scheme — a air sign read through a mutable season.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 29.3° Gemini, Venus was at 24.9° Taurus, Mars was at 12.2° Sagittarius. Read together: a mind at home in argument and pattern; taste for the substantial and the lasting; drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: Venus to Saturn, a trine with 0.3° of slack. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required. Behind it, the Sun sextile Pluto at 0.9°, and Neptune sextile Pluto at 1.3° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, three sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mercury in Gemini at 29.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Venus in Taurus at 24.9° is in domicile; Saturn in Capricorn at 24.6° is in domicile. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 4 air, 3 fire, 2 earth by element and 3 mutable, 3 fixed, 3 cardinal by mode. An air emphasis is read as distance for the sake of clarity: the idea gets examined before it gets adopted. No settled placement falls in water — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Mercury, Mars, Saturn and Neptune were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Capricorn into Aquarius during that day at the birthplace, travelling 13.0° between one midnight and the next. The hour would decide it; no hour was recorded. The reading keeps the question open rather than flipping a coin dressed as astrology.
